Annual Open Call for Cypriot and Cypriot diaspora artists

Applications open · until 10 September

SYNO invites Cypriot and Cypriot diaspora artists to apply to its Open Call.

Shortlisted artists will receive dedicated public profiles on the platform and will be featured through editorial formats, including dialogues with internationally recognized curators and critics. Finalists will also receive an unrestricted cash prize.

Timeline

Applications open14 May
Application deadlineExtended until 10 September
Jury reviewSeptember
Shortlist and finalists announced31 October

Applications closed on 10 September. Selected artists will be announced on 31 October.

Jury

Kyle Dancewicz
Kyle Dancewicz is Deputy Director at SculptureCenter in New York, which he joined in 2016 as Exhibition and Programme Manager. He is also curator of the Cyprus Pavilion at the 61st Venice Biennale.
Hicham Khalidi
Hicham Khalidi has been Director of the Jan van Eyck Academie since 2018. In 2024, he curated the Dutch Pavilion at the 60th International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia. Previously, he worked as Associate Curator at Lafayette Anticipations and held curatorial roles for the Sharjah Biennial, the Biennale of Sydney, and the Marrakech Biennale.
Elena Ketelsen González
Elena Ketelsen González is a curator, writer, and educator currently serving as Associate Curator at MoMA PS1. Previously, she held curatorial and programming positions at the Whitney Museum of American Art, Gracie Mansion Conservancy, and the Museum of the City of New York. She is also the founder of the grassroots curatorial initiative La Salita.
Elena Stylianou
Elena Stylianou is Director of NiMAC and Associate Professor in Art History and Theory at European University Cyprus. She has curated exhibitions including Repetitive Acts, In the Sea of the Setting Sun, and Ar(t)chaeology, and co-edited several important publications on Cypriot contemporary art and visual culture.
Ioulita Toumazi
Ioulita Toumazi is a Cypriot art theorist, curator, and writer. Her texts have appeared in exhibition catalogues, artists’ books, and platforms dedicated to art criticism.

Awards of 3,500 €

Three finalists in each category — emerging and established artists — will be selected, with each receiving an award of 3,500 €.

In addition, up to 10 shortlisted artists will be featured on the website through editorial formats, including dialogues with internationally recognized curators and critics. All shortlisted artists will also be featured in the SYNO Yearbook, to be published by the end of 2026.

FAQ

Who can apply?

The Open Call is open to Cypriot and Cypriot diaspora artists, as well as artists whose practices maintain a meaningful connection to Cyprus. Applicants who are not Cypriot or part of the diaspora are welcome to indicate this relationship within their artist statement

Is there a fee?

No. There is no application fee

Do I need a published artist profile?

No. You can create your profile as you apply. If you’re selected, we’ll publish it with an “Open Call selected” mark

How many works should I submit?

Submit a focused selection of recent works or one significant project, with up to 10 images in total

Can I change my application after sending it?

You can’t edit an application after submitting it. While it’s under review, you can withdraw it and submit a new application before the deadline

Open Call questions
What's your connection to Cyprus?
Born in Limassol and based in Nicosia — the Cypriot coastline is where my practice began and the subject I keep returning to.
Tell us about the works you've selected
The three works come from the same body of research — Tidal Lines and Coastline I were made at the waterline, and Salt Index is the installation they grew out of. Together they trace how the shore holds trade, migration and tide.
Anything else you'd like the jury to know?
The project is site-responsive — I'd adapt the final installation to the exhibition space at NiMAC.
Artist statement

My practice moves between photography and installation, tracing how the Cypriot coastline holds memory — of migration, of trade, of the bodies of water that both divide and connect.

Comely Cad

Elena Andreou

120 × 90 cm
Painting
About

Painted along the Famagusta shoreline across a single winter, the work builds the coast in slow layers of oil and salt-worn light — a study of memory held at the water's edge.

Answers

What's your connection to Cyprus?

Born in Nicosia; based between Cyprus and Berlin. The island's coastline has been the centre of my work since 2022.

Tell us about the works you've selected

The three works come from the same body of research — long-exposure photographs made at the waterline, and the installation of salt-crusted objects they grew out of. Together they trace how the shore holds trade, migration and tide.

Anything else you'd like the jury to know?

The project is site-responsive — I'd adapt the final installation to the exhibition space at NiMAC.

Artist statement

My practice moves between photography and installation, tracing how the Cypriot coastline holds memory — of migration, of trade, of the bodies of water that both divide and connect.
